description: This file defines the CronJobsStore class, a singleton observable object managing scheduled cron jobs within a macOS application. It includes properties for tracking jobs, their status, and associated logs, as well as methods for starting/stopping job refresh cycles, updating jobs, managing gateway events, and handling cron job operations via GatewayConnection. It also handles gateway push notifications relevant to cron events.

classes.name: CronJobsStore
classes.description: A singleton observable class managing cron job scheduling, execution, and status updates. It handles initializing, starting/stopping polling tasks, reacting to gateway push notifications, and providing methods for CRUD operations on cron jobs.

methods.name: start
methods.description: Starts the polling and push notification tasks for updating cron jobs and listening to gateway events.

methods.name: stop
methods.description: Stops all ongoing polling and event listening tasks.

methods.name: refreshJobs
methods.description: Asynchronously refreshes the list of cron jobs and updates scheduler status.

methods.name: refreshRuns
methods.description: Asynchronously refreshes the logs for a specific cron job.

methods.name: runJob
methods.description: Triggers execution of a specific job, optionally forcing it.

methods.name: removeJob
methods.description: Removes a job by ID and refreshes the list if successful.

methods.name: setJobEnabled
methods.description: Enables or disables a specific job.

methods.name: upsertJob
methods.description: Creates or updates a cron job based on provided ID and payload.

methods.name: handle
methods.description: Processes incoming gateway push notifications, especially cron events and sequence gaps, to keep the UI in sync.

methods.name: handle(cronEvent:)
methods.description: Handles cron-specific events, scheduling refreshes accordingly.

methods.name: scheduleRefresh
methods.description: Schedules a delayed refresh of the job list.

methods.name: scheduleRunsRefresh
methods.description: Schedules a delayed refresh of the run log entries for a specific job.
